Recommendation: Functional integration tests for AI-driven weakness-based course recommendations (ExamCourseRecommendationController)
A logged-in learner requests course recommendations based on their own exam attempt, and the result set is capped at 3 courses even if the AI suggested more.
column3:
1. Log in as a LEARNER who has completed at least one exam attempt.
2. Prepare POST /api/v1/exams/ai/recommend-courses body {"examAttemptId":<own attempt id>}.
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect the response body's recommendedCourses[] length and weaknessSummary.
column4: 1. 200 OK; ExamCourseRecommendationAIResponseDTO{examAttemptId, weaknessSummary, recommendedCourses[]} with at most 3 entries, even if the AI suggested more.
column5: - Logged in; caller has ≥1 own exam attempt.

Recommendation: Any authenticated caller can pass ANY examAttemptId — including one belonging to a completely different student — and receive that student's real weakness analysis (confirmed, self-acknowledged IDOR, not fixed).
column3:
1. Log in as User A and complete an exam attempt; note its id.
2. Log out and log in as an unrelated User B.
3. Prepare and send POST /api/v1/exams/ai/recommend-courses body {"examAttemptId":<User A's attempt id>}.
4. Inspect the response and confirm it contains User A's real weakness data.
column4: 1. 200 OK — User B receives User A's real weaknessSummary and recommendedCourses, with no ownership check anywhere in the call chain.
column5: - An exam attempt belonging to a different user (A) exists; caller B is any authenticated user.

Recommendation: An unauthenticated call is rejected with a bare, empty-body 401 — a different shape from every other 401 in the codebase.
column3:
1. Discard any existing Authorization token.
2. Prepare POST /api/v1/exams/ai/recommend-courses with no Authorization header and any valid body.
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect the response status and confirm the body is empty (not JSON).
column4: 1. 401 Unauthorized, with an EMPTY response body (not the usual {"error":...} or ApiErrorDTO JSON shape used elsewhere).

Recommendation: When the AI call fails or returns unparseable output, the endpoint gracefully degrades to a 200 with empty results rather than surfacing a 500/502/503.
column3:
1. Arrange a test environment where Gemini is unavailable or misconfigured (e.g. an invalid API key).
2. Log in and prepare POST /api/v1/exams/ai/recommend-courses with a valid examAttemptId.
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect the response status and body.
column4: 1. 200 OK; weaknessSummary="" and recommendedCourses=[] — always 200, never propagated as an error status.
column5: - A way to simulate an AI failure; a valid examAttemptId.

Recommendation: There is no role restriction at all on this endpoint — TRAINER, COURSE_MANAGER, and ADMINISTRATOR accounts can all call it successfully, unlike the stricter gating on Learning Pathway/AI Assistant.
column3:
1. Log in as a TRAINER with access to a valid exam attempt id and call the endpoint; inspect the response.
2. Repeat as a COURSE_MANAGER.
3. Repeat as an ADMINISTRATOR.
4. Confirm all three calls succeed identically.
column4: 1. All three succeed 200 OK — confirming zero @PreAuthorize/role gate exists on this controller.
column5: - Each role has access to at least one exam attempt id.

2. Inspect the resulting recommendedCourses[] entry for that id.
column4: 1. The corresponding RecommendedCourseDTO entry has empty-string title/category/difficulty rather than being filtered out of the response.
column5: - A reproducible way to make the AI return an invalid course id (may require test-double/prompt manipulation).

Recommendation: KNOWN OPEN GAP (not fixed): if even ONE AI-recommended course has a malformed (non-numeric) courseId, the parse failure discards the ENTIRE otherwise-valid response — including weaknessSummary and the other, correctly-formed recommendations — because it throws inside the same try block guarded by the broad catch-all also used for real AI/network failures. This is distinct from RECOMMENDATION_FT08 (a numerically-valid but stale/non-existent id), which degrades gracefully per-entry instead.
column3:
1. (Best-effort/hard to force deterministically — requires a test-double/prompt manipulation to make the AI return a non-numeric courseId, e.g. courseId:"abc" or courseId:null for one of the 3 recommendations, while the other 2 and weaknessSummary are well-formed.) Trigger such a response.
2. Inspect the full response body.
column4: 1. 200 OK, but weaknessSummary="" and recommendedCourses=[] — the entire response silently degrades to the AI-failure fallback shape (ExamCourseRecommendationAIService.recommendCoursesAI's Long.parseLong(String.valueOf(courseId)) throws NumberFormatException inside the try block, caught by the same catch (Exception e) branch as real Gemini failures), losing the 2 otherwise-valid recommendations and the weaknessSummary text along with the 1 bad entry. NOT FIXED — flag as a real, still-open bug; do not silently patch production code for this.
